title.narrative: Skills for Employment Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The investment program will support the Government of Bangladesh's reforms in skills development, anchored in the National Skills Development Policy (NSDP), 2011. It will support large-scale private sector involvement and public-private partnership, which is critical to meet existing and future labor market needs and to reduce the skills gap. This in turn is crucial for Bangladesh to move away from the 'low-skill, low-wage equilibriumm' to a 'higher skill, higher wage virtuous cycle' to become a middle income country. The program will help the government to scale-up skilling of new entrants and up-skilling of existing workers to contribute to higher growth of priority sectors. The program will strengthen skills development in Bangladesh and support transition to a sector-wide approach (SWAp) by establishing a unified funding system and enhancing overall coordination of the currently fragmented system.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Increased employment in priority sectors and skills for males and females [NSDP 2 and 3].

Annual share of higher skills training in priority sector increased by 15% (Baseline: 3% increased annually) Achievement: 22.39 Progress/Status: Annual share of higher skills training experienced 1.1% increase in 2015 and 0.9% in 2016 compared to the previous years. It has reduced over years mainly due to basic skills training capacity has been growing much faster than higher skills training capacity.
Enrollment in mid and higher level courses on 31 March 2021, was 55,939 which is 22.39% of total enrollment. Data Source: • Labor Force Surveys • Trainee Management System • Quarterly progress reports

Annual share of certified trainees increased by 10% (Baseline: 5%) Achievement: 10.5 Progress/Status: The growth of certified trainees was 45.2% during 2014-2015 and 19.8% during 2015-2016.
SEIP certification has increased by 5.85% from December 2019 to December 2020. The number of certified trainees on 31 December 2019 was 252,268 (30.56% or 77,094 female) and 267,040 (29.30% or 78,249 female) on 31 December 2020. The number is same as of 31 March 2021 also. Data Source: • Labor Force Surveys • Trainee Management System • Quarterly progress reports

Annual skills training capacity in priority sectors increased by 10% (Baseline: 5% increased annually) Achievement: 49.11 Progress/Status: Skills training capacity in priority sectors increased by 45.2% during 2014-2015 and by 19.8% during 2015-2016.
Enrollment under T1 of the SEIP did not increase during the last one year as T1 activities ended on 31 December 2019. The number of enrollments at the end of December 2019 was 279,748 and that on December 2020 was also 279,748 i.e. no growth during the last one year under T1. Out of the above enrollment 80,463 were female (28.76%). Training activities under Tranche 1 completed in December 2019. Data Source: • Labor Force Surveys • Trainee Management System • Quarterly progress reports

Annual share of disadvantaged groups in skills training increased by 10% (Baseline: 8%) Achievement: 79 Progress/Status: SEIP's enrollment of disadvantaged trainees (Ethnic Minority, Physically Challenged and extremely Poor) as of 31 March 2021, is 220,680 or 78.9% of total enrollment. Out of this, 215,956 were poor, 3,918 ethnic community members and 806 physically challenged. Data Source: • Labor Force Surveys • Trainee Management System • Quarterly progress reports
